sentences.text: Matanas enrighti was an extinct duck that lived in New Zealand during the Miocene epoch.

Scientists described the species based on a left humerus fossil found at the Saint Bathans Fauna site near Mata Creek in the Central Otago region of New Zealand's South Island, collected from the lower Bannockburn Formation of the Manuherikia Group.
The specific epithet enrighti honors Jack Enright, the owner of the station where the type material was collected.
Worthy and colleagues formally named this species in 2007.
Taxonomically, Matanas belongs to the family Anatidae and is placed within the subfamily Anatini.
This duck lived between 18.7 and 15.9 million years ago, spanning the Burdigalian and Langhian stages.
